key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray process control can help tailor protective coatings for steel components exposed to corrosion and humidity-dependent sliding wear.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, lamellar structure, and coating porosity.
Evaluate corrosion and sliding wear against Si3N4 balls under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and lower friction coefficients and wear rates as humidity increases, without numerical results.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear findings involve Si3N4 counterfaces and may not generalize to other contact materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
